# Attachment Rules

Reusable functions for checking parent–instruction compatibility and compiling attachment action hooks. It inherits Party Access Functions for activation, caller authority and reader-access checks. Validation results and compiled bindings do not themselves establish that an attachment was installed or an action completed.

## Identity and parties

`origin(document)` returns the Blue identity of the supplied document’s `/contracts/initialized/document`. It rejects a missing initialized document.

`checkRoster(parent, child, authority, cross)` checks role-keyed party maps:

- `parent` must contain at least one party, and every parent role must appear in `child`.
- For each shared role, `samePrimary(left, right)` requires both `lead/channel` values to exist and have identical Blue identities. Their `readerKeys` must be nonempty, duplicate-free and equal regardless of order. Missing `readerKeys` are treated as empty for this check and cannot satisfy it.
- The only additional child role permitted is `authority`, which must appear in `child`. When `cross` is true, it must also appear in `parent`.

These primary-party comparisons do not require matching representative rosters.

## Compiling hooks

`compileHooks(allowed, hooks, key)` accepts `hooks` organized by action name, then hook name. Every action must appear in `allowed`. Hook names use `validPartyName`: nonempty text containing none of `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. Original and generated hook names must not collide within an action.

Each hook selects its source with `in` and `on`:

- `in` defaults to `instruction`; the only other permitted value is `parent`.
- `on` defaults to `workflow`. Instruction-local hooks require `workflow`.
- Parent hooks require an explicit `on: state` or `on: event`. Event hooks must contain `event`. State hooks must contain `path` beginning with `/` and an `equals` value.

Parent hooks become `on: embedded` bindings at `/sources/parent`. A parent state hook matches a `Source Changed` event whose `attachment` is `key` and whose `hook` is the action name and hook name joined by `_`. Its condition checks the current parent value at `path` against `equals`, together with the supplied `when`, which defaults to true. Receiving the event alone does not establish that the state condition holds.

Every parent hook also checks that the parent still selects this instruction’s initialized identity. The selection uses `/clauses/attachment/parameters/instructionPath` within `/sources/parent`, followed by `/contracts/initialized/document`; that selected node must exist and match the executing instruction’s `/contracts/initialized/document` by Blue identity.

Before any supplied `before` effects, generated guards require:

- `/sources/parent/activation/active` to equal true;
- the role named by `/clauses/attachment/parameters/authority` to remain in `/sources/parent/activation/parties`;
- every parent role’s primary channel identity and reader-key count and membership to match the corresponding party in the instruction’s `/activation/parties`.

Failures reject the hook attempt. Supplied `before` effects follow these guards; an absent `before` contributes an empty list. Other supplied hook configuration, including `params` and `after`, is retained except where compilation replaces source, event or condition fields.

The result contains:

- `bindings`: compiled hooks grouped by action;
- `signals`: parent-state notification descriptors with `id` and the original parent `path`;
- `parentDependencies`: each parent hook’s `action`, `hook`, original `on` and original `path`, defaulting the recorded path to an empty string when absent;
- `relationship`: `cross-embedded` when any parent hook exists, otherwise `one-way`.

These are returned descriptions; `compileHooks` does not emit the described signals.

## State rechecks

`recheckOn` defaults to an empty list and must be a list. Explicitly supplying it, even empty, is allowed only for a parent state hook and forbids supplying either `before` or `after`.

Each recheck path must begin with `/`, must not be `/`, must not begin with `/sources`, and must be unique within that hook. These paths refer to the executing instruction’s own document. Each creates an additional `on: change` binding named `<hookName>_recheck_<index>`, starting at index zero. It retains the parent selection, state equality, `when` and generated parent guards, allowing a local change to reconsider the parent-state condition without another parent event.

For hooks explicitly supplying `recheckOn`, `checkStateExpression(expression)` examines `params` (default `{}`) and `when` (default true). It rejects any nested object field named `$event`, `$binding`, `$var`, `$resultValue`, `$call`, `$const`, `$steps`, `$currentContract`, `$intrinsic`, `$events` or `$changeset`. Traversal that remains unfinished after 32 passes is rejected as too deep.

## Caller, activation and access

`requireCaller()` requires the binding `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to equal true, otherwise rejecting with `ATTACHMENT_EXACT_REVIEW_REQUIRED`. It then invokes `requireActive` with `call/channel` and `workflow: true`.

`requireActive(channel, workflow)` performs its activation checks only when `/activation` exists. In that case, `active` must pass the check, with absence defaulting to false, and participant access must pass `accessValid`. When `workflow` is true, `authority(channel, state)` must also recognize the channel name as a current party role or a current representative name in the form `<role>__<repId>`. Failed checks reject with `DOCUMENT_NOT_ACTIVE`, `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING` or `REPRESENTATIVE_NO_LONGER_AUTHORIZED`, respectively. An absent `/activation` skips these checks; it is not evidence of an active state.

The inherited access helpers work as follows:

- `readerGroups(readers, roster)` combines additional reader groups with each party’s and representative’s `readerKeys`. Roster-derived groups replace additional groups with the same name. Missing `readerKeys` contribute empty groups; absent `representatives` contribute none.
- `transports(roster)` collects each party’s `lead/channel` and each representative’s `channel`, using role names and `<role>__<repId>` names.
- `accessValid(accessPaths, readers, roster)` resolves the listed access-document paths in the executing document and delegates to `accessRecordsValid(accessDocuments, readers, roster)`.
- `accessRecordsValid` skips External Channel transports. Every other transport must be a Timeline Channel. For each such channel, one Timeline Access document must name the exact timeline, match its provider, and include at least one key from every reader group in `allowedKeys`. An empty reader group cannot satisfy this check. Coverage split across multiple access documents is insufficient for a single channel’s check. Examined access records must be Timeline Access documents.

Within `requireActive`, absent `accessPaths`, `readers` and `parties` default to an empty list, empty map and empty map respectively. These checks inspect access-document state; confirmed Timeline Access permissions depend on provider publication and executed history. Read access does not confer publishing or business-operation authority.

Separately, `businessReady()` returns true when `/activation` is absent. Otherwise it requires `closed` to be false (default false), approval for every role in `required` (default empty list; missing approvals default false), current agreed terms and valid participant access. `termsCurrent()` compares each document path recorded in `/activation/terms/fields` with its stored agreed value; absent `fields` defaults to an empty map. These readiness checks return a Boolean and do not activate the document or grant caller authority.
